findings.scenario: Attacker generates a fresh ed25519 key (free), reaches UDP 4433 (the documented firewall opens it to the whole 100.96.0.0/12 mesh, or to the Internet if listen_addr is public), completes QUIC + HLO1 and is registered as a peer. (a) Write: open a stream with magic TXFR and header {project_id: '<id seen in any gossip topic project/<id>>', file_id: 'scripts/convert.py' or '.cargo/config.toml', version: 999}; handle_incoming_transfer resolves the path (only the first segment '.synergos' is blocked), accepts because no local record is stale/conflicting, and atomically replaces the file in the member's working tree; every other member auto-pulls it. (b) Read: send signed FileWant{version:0} for guessed/observed paths; handle_file_want pushes the current version, and history nodes serve every retained version via serve_from_history. No step consults a membership list, invite, Cernere identity, or control-plane registry.
findings.impact_ai_game: Unreleased game assets, model checkpoints and datasets are exfiltrable by anyone with mesh reach, and working trees on every node (artist laptops, build/CI nodes, history nodes) can be poisoned, including tool-config files that lead to RCE. For AI training data it means silent dataset corruption replicated to every node with no provenance.
findings.current_state: Authentication = possession of any ed25519 key; authorization = none. The invite token is explicitly documented as 'not an authorization boundary'; the mesh firewall/Cloudflare WARP membership is the only control, and the control plane registry is never consumed by the daemon.
findings.proposed_redesign: Introduce a membership credential as the data-plane authorization primitive: (1) Cernere/control plane records org -> project -> node membership; (2) the control plane issues per-node short-lived membership certificates (SPIFFE-style X.509 or Biscuit tokens: {org, project_ids[], node pubkey, device posture claim, exp <= 1h, kid}); (3) QUIC uses mTLS with the node's ed25519 cert and the membership cert is presented in the handshake extension or first stream; (4) accept() verifies the chain against the control-plane root key and installs a per-connection capability set; (5) dispatch_peer_streams checks (peer, project) in caps BEFORE reading a TXFR/BSW1/GSP1 body (header peek + stream reset on deny), handle_file_want/serve_from_history check the requester's caps, gossip subscriptions are built per peer from caps; (6) nodes fetch a signed revocation/allowlist bundle every <= 60 s and fail closed when stale. Data model: ProjectMembership{org_id, project_id, peer_id, role(reader|writer|history), issued_at, exp, revoked_at}; wire: HLO2/mTLS + MembershipCert; config: `require_membership = true` default.
alternatives: Per-project pre-shared symmetric key carried in HLO1: trivial to implement but no per-node revocation, any member compromise leaks the key, no Cernere linkage.
Rely on Cloudflare Mesh / Tailscale grants only: cannot express project-level granularity, direct P2P/relay paths bypass it, and it contradicts the org rule that auth centralizes in Cernere.
Host-signed membership list gossiped by the project owner: works offline but duplicates identity outside Cernere and has no device posture.
sources: research/breach-containment.md §1.1 (NIST SP 800-207 per-connection, dynamic policy), §1.3 (Biscuit offline attenuation, revocation ids), §1.4 (SPIRE 1h SVID TTL), §5.3 (kill switch), catalogue P0-1/P0-2
research/vcs-game-ai.md §1.2 (Perforce protections: path x principal x host with explicit deny), §1.5 (CVE-2026-6043: insecure default = everyone is super until first p4 protect)

findings.scenario: Victim V bootstraps to any node M (an invite's peer_info_url, a bootstrap_url, or a legitimately joined peer that is later compromised). As the server side, M receives V's SignedHello blob. M then connects to server S and sends the identical blob: verify() checks only the static signature (ts_ms is never compared to the clock, there is no server nonce or TLS exporter binding), so S registers M's QUIC connection under V's PeerId and `insert` silently replaces V's genuine entry. S's outbound FileOffer pushes and FileWant answers for V now go to M, and M's inbound TXFR/gossip streams are attributed to V. Any future allowlist keyed by PeerId (SEC-AZ-01) is bypassed unless this is fixed first.
findings.impact_ai_game: Identity spoofing defeats membership enforcement, audit attribution ('who pushed this asset/version') and conflict detection; a compromised contractor node can impersonate a lead's node to every peer it has ever talked to.
findings.current_state: Server-side TLS pinning is one-way (no client cert); client identity rests solely on the HLO1 signature over (peer_id, pubkey, ts_ms); docs/operations-readiness claims mutual authentication.
findings.proposed_redesign: Bind identity to the session: use TLS client certificates (self-signed ed25519, SPKI pinned exactly like the server side) so the handshake itself proves key possession; if HLO1 is kept as metadata, sign (domain tag 'synergos/hello/v1' || server nonce || TLS exporter value (RFC 8446 exporter / RFC 9266 style channel binding) || ts_ms) and reject |now - ts_ms| > 120 s. Duplicate PeerId policy: a second connection for an existing PeerId must pass the fresh challenge and then explicitly closes the old one with a logged security event; never a blind overwrite. Add ALPN 'synergos/1' to version the handshake.
alternatives: Server nonce only, no channel binding: stops offline replay but a relay/MITM can still forward a live hello.
Noise-IK style handshake inside QUIC streams: duplicates what TLS already provides.
sources: research/breach-containment.md §1.1 (per-connection auth), §1.4 (short-lived SVIDs)

findings.scenario: (a) A token pasted into Slack/Discord is forwarded or scraped; it has no use counter, the host never learns it was used, and the CLI default is no expiry, so anyone holding it weeks later joins (and with SEC-AZ-01 becomes a full member). (b) An attacker crafts a token whose project_id equals the victim's real project id and whose peer_info_url points at the attacker; the victim's daemon silently reuses the already-open local project and registers the attacker's node as a peer of it, after which the attacker receives that project's offers and can push into it.
findings.impact_ai_game: Onboarding external vendors and AI-pipeline nodes by chat-pasted tokens is the normal workflow in studios; unbounded bearer invites are exactly the Rockstar/Okta-class credential path and make NDA scoping impossible.
findings.current_state: syn1 tokens are host-signed JSON with optional expiry and an unused nonce; verification is entirely on the joiner; legacy UUID tokens are one-shot but daemon-local only.
findings.proposed_redesign: Invite = single-use, invitee-bound, host-consumed: payload {project_ref, host_peer_id, invitee (Cernere user id or invitee pubkey), nonce, exp <= 24h default, scope(role)}; join becomes a JOIN1 stream to the host: joiner sends {token, joiner pubkey, signature}; host checks nonce unused (persistent ledger), expiry, invitee binding, then issues the membership credential (SEC-AZ-01) and records the join in the control plane. Project identity must be namespaced (project_ref = blake3(org_id || host_pubkey || local_id)) so a token cannot alias an existing local project; the UI must show org/host before joining.
alternatives: Keep bearer tokens but add a mandatory TTL and a control-plane use counter: cheaper, still leakable within the window.
Cernere-mediated invites only (no offline tokens): cleanest identity story but blocks air-gapped LAN onboarding.
sources: research/breach-containment.md §1.4 (GitHub fine-grained PAT max lifetime, 5-min OIDC exchange), §6 (Okta HAR-token theft)

findings.scenario: A peer that is legitimately connected for project B (or any peer, given SEC-AZ-01) publishes on topic project/A: a FileOffer makes every A member auto-pull the attacker's bytes (eligibility is only 'project open and version not held'); ConflictAlert{file_id} creates phantom conflicts with no signer check; PeerStatus{peer_id: <lead>, Offline} marks other peers disconnected because origin is ignored. In the reverse direction, because the mesh is always empty, project A's FileOffer/FileWant/CatalogUpdate (paths, sizes, CRCs, catalog CIDs) are fanned out to every QUIC connection including peers that only belong to project B.
findings.impact_ai_game: Multi-client studios and NDA'd vendor projects leak file names and catalog metadata across projects; attackers can trigger pulls of poisoned assets and disrupt presence/conflict UI used by leads.
findings.current_state: Envelope signature + signer == self-declared sender for 3 of 5 variants; no subscription or membership check on receive; one-hop delivery; fan-out fallback to all connections.
findings.proposed_redesign: Authorization at the gossip edge: (1) each connection carries an authorized topic set derived from the membership credential (SEC-AZ-01); handle_gossip_stream drops frames whose topic is not authorized for the sender and logs a security event; (2) every variant carries `origin` and verify() binds it to the signer (ConflictAlert gains origin + project_id; CatalogUpdate publisher becomes mandatory, legacy empty-publisher path removed); (3) PeerStatus may only describe origin's own state; (4) fan-out uses only peers authorized for the topic, never the all-connections fallback; (5) per-(origin, topic) sequence numbers plus a bounded replay window replace the 1000-entry message cache as replay protection; (6) canonical length-prefixed signing bytes.
alternatives: Per-project gossip encryption keys (members-only readability) without authorization checks: hides content but still allows injection by any member and key rotation on leave is hard.
Full libp2p gossipsub with peer scoring: heavier, still needs the membership oracle.

DhtRequest::Announce { record } => { let peer_id = record.peer_id.clone(); ... self.announce(PeerRecord::from_dto(record)).await; self.add_peer(peer_id, endpoints, None).await; DhtResponse::AnnounceAck }
DhtRequest::FindProjectPeers { project_id } => { let peers = self.find_project_peers(&project_id).await ... DhtResponse::ProjectPeers { peers } }

findings.scenario: Any connected peer sends Announce{record: {peer_id: <victim>, endpoints: [attacker addr], active_projects: [every id], ttl_secs: u64::MAX}}; the receiver stores it and overwrites the victim's routing entry, then serves it to third parties via FindNode/FindProjectPeers. FindProjectPeers{project_id} returns membership and display_name to anyone. The production DHT client is dormant today, so this is a latent trap for the intended discovery design rather than a live exploit.
findings.impact_ai_game: Eclipse/poisoning of discovery lets an attacker insert itself as the 'publisher' of assets or a 'history node'; membership disclosure violates NDA boundaries and the no-personal-data rule (display_name).
findings.current_state: Records are unsigned DTOs; the stream handler does not receive the authenticated sender; no admission or Sybil cost.
findings.proposed_redesign: Signed peer records (libp2p-style): {peer_id, pubkey, endpoints, projects, seq, exp} signed by the record's key; Announce accepted only if signer == record.peer_id == authenticated stream sender and seq is monotonic; TTL capped; FindProjectPeers requires the caller's membership credential for that project and returns no display_name; routing table admission limited to credentialed peers. If a public DHT is not a product goal, delete the DHT and use the control-plane registry as the discovery oracle.
alternatives: Keep DHT private to the mesh and rely on SEC-AZ-01 admission only: simpler, but records remain spoofable within the mesh.

findings.scenario: A project member (or any peer, per SEC-AZ-01) pushes `scripts/convert.py` through the normal receive path (only the `.synergos/` prefix is refused). On every node whose daemon config has the documented post-receive hook, the next received PNG triggers `python scripts/convert.py` as the daemon user with the daemon's environment (identity passphrase, node key, AWS/GDrive rotation credentials). With allow_project_hooks=true, a committed `.synergos/hooks.toml` runs on every project the daemon opens, re-read per event with no hash pin or approval.
findings.impact_ai_game: Asset pipelines rely on converters/linters; this turns the asset store into the Maya scriptNode worm pattern (an outsourcer's push executes on every studio node and history/CI node).

findings.scenario: Curare's per-route checks are correct today (download/plan always resolve blobRef from asset_versions after a 'download' permission check), so there is no direct IDOR; the problem is that custody has no second opinion. Any future Curare bug or compromise that lets a user name a blobRef (e.g. a route resembling /storage/receipts) yields a download capability for any tenant's object, because custody only checks 'the global token holder asked'. The custody token leak = `reclaim` of every object with permanent tombstones. Because Curare holds receipt_secret, Curare (or anyone with its env) can forge 'durable' receipts, so a receipt proves nothing to a third party. Capabilities are replayable until expiry from any IP and leak via proxy/CDN query-string logs.
findings.impact_ai_game: Custody is meant to be the durable anchor for release artifacts and datasets; a single symmetric secret shared with the web tier means one web-tier breach is total loss of confidentiality and durability guarantees across all orgs.

alternatives: Keep HMAC everywhere but add domain-separation prefixes and kids: cheap, fixes rotation and cross-use, does not fix forgeability by Curare.
Custody validates a Curare session via token introspection on every GET: strongest binding, adds a round trip per transfer and couples custody availability to Curare.

findings.scenario: After a suspected leak, nobody can answer 'which user received download URLs for which versions', 'who granted manage to whom', 'who reclaimed object X', 'who purged the history store', or 'which admin reissued the node key' - the checklist item '管理者操作に対する監査ログ' is unmet on every surface, and exfiltration-volume analytics (mass download alerts) have no data source.
findings.impact_ai_game: Studios subject to TPN/MPA or AI-Act documentation duties need per-asset access evidence; without it, the platform cannot support incident response or compliance attestations.
findings.current_state: Structured request logs without principal; domain_events outbox exists but is write-only; custody and control emit nothing per operation.
findings.proposed_redesign: A shared audit event schema {ts, actor (Cernere uuid or node id), service, action, target (org/project/asset/version/object), outcome, request_id, capability_id} written append-only (Curare: `access_events` table; custody/control: JSONL + shipped) into a Merkle history tree with daily checkpoints exported to the immutable replica tier and to the customer org; alerting on per-identity volume baselines. Retention policy per org rule (UUIDs only, no PII).
alternatives: Plain append-only tables without tamper evidence: adequate for forensics, not for proving the vendor did not alter logs.

coverage_notes: Read all 11 available maps and the 4 research notes in full (source-URL appendices of the research notes were skimmed). The map sy-clients-docs.md never appeared: checked before code work and again after the first verification batch (two retries); the Tauri GUI, Dioxus admin UI client code, ars plugin and user-facing Synergos docs were therefore NOT independently audited for auth boundaries beyond what sy-control-custody.md covered (admin UI session/token handling). Every finding's evidence lines were re-read from source during this pass; where a claim rests on a map line I did not re-open (e.g. absolute-path leak in build_catalog_snapshot, AWS credentials in hook env via s3.rs) it is phrased as reported by the map. Scope covered per the lens: synergos-control admin/node/org APIs and token issuance; custody admin API and HMAC transfer URLs; /peer-info; relay join; IPC uid/SID checks and privileged commands; gossip/DHT authenticity and membership; hook registration/execution; Curare routes (upload/confirm/download, acquisition plan, versions/pins, logical-assets grants, projects, submissions/decisions, releases, identity, shared-nodes, synergos proxy, storage operations, workflow/assignments); Cernere WS verification and dev header; grant revocation after除名; Web UI token handling; Cu->Sy confused deputy. IDOR check: no direct cross-tenant IDOR found on object routes (ids are resolved then checked against the owning logical asset's scope+grant); residual issues are the 404/403 oracle, unvalidated ids and member-visible internals (SEC-AZ-16/21). CSRF is not applicable (Bearer-only auth, CORS restricted to FRONTEND_URL). Not done: no tests were executed, no live Cernere/Sy/Cu endpoints exercised, Windows-specific IPC code not built, relay production wiring assumed dormant per the discovery map. Findings on rate limiting/body limits, supply chain, and encryption at rest are left to the other security lenses except where they intersect auth (SEC-AZ-14).
